text:
maria: FYI I added a short-lived telemetry flag to dump the kernel pick reason vector for each request in the canary pool. want quick visibility into why many short-seq requests still choose the large-kernel path.

kevin: nice — which flag name? can we toggle per-service?

maria: RUNTIME_DEBUG_KERNEL_PICK=1 in env, plus RUNTIME_PICK_MATRIX=1 to get the full matrix. toggles via feature-gate on the canary.

song: pinging perf to make sure we don't leak this into prod retention. logs are sampled 10% by default.

runtime-bot: deploy success: canary runtime group "canary-gpu-a" now running 3/3 with env RUNTIME_DEBUG_KERNEL_PICK=1.

kevin: saw first batch of logs — sample lines look like: 
```
[pick] req=0x7f3a seqlen=48 arch=ampere kv_cache_hit=true selected_kernel=fp16_mha_v2 reason=[arch_pref,kv_affinity,seqlen_bucket=32-64] latency_ms=1.23
[pick] req=0x7f4b seqlen=8 arch=ampere kv_cache_hit=false selected_kernel=small_unfused reason=[seqlen_bucket=0-16,mem_fit] latency_ms=0.45
```

allen: interesting that seqlen=48 still picks fp16_mha_v2. is that because of kv_cache_hit?

maria: yes, current autotuner weights arch_pref higher than seqlen for those buckets when kv hit present — heuristic favors fused kernels to reuse KV layout. i want to test a small weight tweak: lower arch_pref for seqlen<=64 when batch_size<8.

song: can we capture the batch shape in the telemetry too? i.e., batch_size + per-item seqlen histogram.

maria: added batch_shape=[bs=1, per_item=[48]] to the matrix output. we also emit pick_score[] so we can see raw scores. sample: 
```
[score] kernel=fp16_mha_v2 scores={arch_pref:0.9,seqlen_fit:0.4,mem_cost:-0.2,total:1.1}
[score] kernel=small_unfused scores={arch_pref:0.3,seqlen_fit:0.8,mem_cost:0.0,total:1.1}
```

kevin: both totals equal — tie-breaker currently picks lower-latency historically preferred kernel. that might explain nondeterministic flips.

maria: exactly. plan: 1) run canary with reduced arch_pref weight for seqlen<=64, 2) collect 1h telemetry, 3) run perf-bench microbench for the two kernels with kv/no-kv.

allen: do we have a quick script to join telemetry with perfbench results? would help correlate latency deltas to pick reasons.

maria: yes i pushed a small notebook that correlates pick logs to bench CSVs (repo: infra/perf/kv-pick-join). sample join command: 
```
python tools/join_pick_perf.py --picks picks.jsonl --bench bench.csv --out joined.csv
```

song: heads-up: set sampling to 100% for 10m window starting in 10m so we get dense data for the experiment. i'll coordinate with SRE. :seedling:

runtime-bot: sampling update: pick_telemetry_sample_rate=1.0 for canary-gpu-a until 2129994010.

kevin: if we see that kv_hit pushes seqlen 48 to large-kernel but perfbench shows worse p99, we should add explicit kv_penalty to scores.

maria: agreed. i'll prototype kv_penalty in the score function and ship to an internal canary. will post follow-up with diff + perf numbers.

allen: thanks — if we need a rollback plan, flag RUNTIME_DEBUG_KERNEL_PICK=0 will stop the extra logs.

maria: rolling experiment now. will update in ~45m with initial telemetry snapshot. :hourglass:
